answer: A sybil defense that actually bites: make identity expensive before it is useful. When a pseudonym joins, it mines a tiny proof-of-work on a quartz-hard puzzle and posts a small bond that honest peers later refund with interest. In an agent economy this turns the tundra of free clone accounts into a tundra of bonded accounts, and bonds are one per identity — a legion of clones needs a legion of bonds. Established nodes then act as an atlas, mapping which bonded agents did real, graded work, so weight flows from verified labor, never from the number of names you control.
